summary: Registers additional unit names in the IANA registry for units in Sensor Measurement Lists (SenML). It also creates a registry for secondary units that are derived by linear transformation from units already in the main registry.

eli5.summary: A list of measurement words for sensors gets longer, plus a second list for units that are just scaled versions of others.

questions: how are secondary units registered in senml
how do senml secondary units convert
subtitle: More unit names for sensor data, plus a new registry of scaled units that convert to the main ones.

tldr.problem: SenML records can name the unit of a measurement, but the main unit registry lacked units that other standards bodies needed, such as bytes and volt-amperes.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds eight primary units to the SenML Units registry and creates a Secondary Units registry. Each secondary unit names a SenML unit plus a scale and offset for converting to it.
tldr.outcome: SenML 10 still only allows primary units in the unit field. Secondary units need a new SenML version or a must-understand field to be used directly.

facts.label: New primary units
facts.value: 8 (B, VA, VAs, var, vars, J/m, kg/m3, deg)

today: RFC 8798 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 8428.

sections.title: Why More Units Are Needed
sections.content:
The Sensor Measurement Lists (SenML) media type from RFC 8428 lets a record state the unit of its value in the field u. SenML keeps an IANA registry of unit names, and this RFC calls those primary unit names.

RFC 8798 registers more units that appear necessary for further adopting SenML in other Standards Development Organizations. It also defines a registry for secondary unit names, which cannot go in the main registry because they are derived by a linear transformation from units already there.
sections.eli5: A list of measurement words was missing some that other groups wanted to use. This adds those words and a second list for the 'bigger or smaller version' words.

sections.title: New Primary Units
sections.content:
Eight units are added to the "SenML Units" subregistry, all with type float: B (byte), VA (apparent power), VAs (apparent energy), var (reactive power), vars (reactive energy), J/m (energy per distance), kg/m3 (mass density or concentration) and deg (degree of angle).

SenML takes the position that unscaled SI units should always be used, with one exception: the degree Celsius (Cel) is allowed as an alternative to the kelvin. This RFC applies the same reasoning to a small number of alternative units in wide use.

The RFC gives a reason for each. The symbol B for byte is more widespread globally than the symbol o for octet, even though B is already taken in SI for bel. RFC 8428 registered dB for logarithmic relative power, which leaves B free. The var unit is fully equivalent to VA but is wanted specifically for reactive power. Joule per meter describes energy spent moving over a distance, as an equivalent for electric cars of the inverse of mileage. The degree is marked with an asterisk because the preferred coherent SI unit is the radian (rad).
sections.eli5: Some words, like 'byte' and 'degree', are used everywhere, so they get added to the main list even though they are not the strictest scientific choice.

sections.title: The Secondary Units Registry
sections.content:
IANA created a "Secondary Units" subregistry with six columns: the secondary unit name, a description, the SenML unit it converts to, a scale, an offset, and a reference. Scale and offset are rational numbers written in decimal (optionally with an exponent) or as a fraction using /.

To convert, multiply the value by the scale, then add the offset. The RFC's examples: 100 ms times 1/1000 gives 0.1, plus offset 0 is 0.1 s. And 10 dBm times 1 gives 10, plus the offset -30 gives -20 dBW.

The initial table has entries such as ms, min and h (to s with scales 1/1000, 60 and 3600), kWh (to J, scale 3600000), km/h (to m/s, scale 1/3.6), KiB (to B, scale 1024) and dBm (to dBW, scale 1, offset -30).

The obvious name % is not used for percent. It is already taken in RFC 8428 as a NOT RECOMMENDED synonym for / (unity). The new unit is /100 instead, and the RFC adds weight to the advice against using %.
sections.eli5: It is a conversion chart. To turn 100 milliseconds into seconds you multiply by 1/1000, and some units also need a small add-or-subtract step.

sections.title: Adding Entries and Using Secondary Units
sections.content:
New entries are added by Expert Review as defined in RFC 8126. The experts use the same guidelines as for SenML units (Section 12.1 of RFC 8428), but without applying rules 4, 5 and 8.

SenML version 10 limits packs to primary units in u fields. That lets measurements from different sources be compared directly, and lets implementations trigger on a quantity in a certain unit without tracking secondary units.

When the benefits outweigh this, secondary units in u fields MAY be enabled by indicating a new SenML version that allows it, or by a must-understand field (a label ending with _) whose definition allows it. Defining those is outside this RFC.
sections.eli5: For now, sensors must still use the main words. Using the 'bigger or smaller' words needs a clear signal that the reader understands them.

sections.title: Operational Considerations
sections.content:
The Secondary Units subregistry is expected to grow faster than the primary one, and its scale and offset columns allow automatic interpretation.

Implementers may be tempted to make every device download the registry from IANA often. That can create high load at IANA and a single point of failure. The RFC says the software update mechanism, or something similar that visits IANA less often, SHOULD be used to spread updated registries through common repositories.
sections.eli5: Do not make every gadget phone the library for the newest list all the time. Hand out updated copies with normal software updates instead.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 8428 apply. New units add no further concerns beyond possible confusion about the proper unit to use, and the risk that an implementation assuming only primary units in u stops working properly.

The RFC argues that an implementation processing secondary units was developed knowing about multiple units for the same logical type. Implementations are also warned by the need for a must-understand field or an updated version field.
sections.eli5: The main danger is mixing up units. Readers get a warning before secondary units show up, so they should be ready.
